summary: Tested AI Taproom landing both backend (pytest) and frontend (Playwright) end-to-end with focus on new scroll-driven pinned hero cut, section transitions, and form submissions. All 9 backend tests pass (100%). Frontend: hero overlay (3D-rendered taproom with brand mark + SCROLL TO CUT cue) renders over dark scene; scroll-driven blade cut animates with depth parallax; real hero (headline, CTAs) is revealed at end of pin; scrolling back to top reassembles overlay (SCROLL TO CUT visible again). Waitlist and Event booking forms submit successfully end-to-end (success states with WhatsApp CTA & 'You're in' message observed). No horizontal overflow at 1440x900 or 390x844. No console errors.
critical_code_review_comments: Hero.jsx uses many useTransform calls — acceptable but keep an eye on perf on low-end mobile; consider prefers-reduced-motion fallback for the 8-blade scroll cut.
server.py waitlist/bookings rely on E11000 for duplicate detection; works but a pre-check query on email+event_id would be clearer and avoids relying on a unique index being present in prod.
seed_data_creation: Created a few TEST_ prefixed waitlist entries and one TEST_ booking during API/UI testing (not cleaned up since the DB belongs to test_database and no cleanup endpoint exists; entries are clearly TEST_ prefixed).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Hero is intentionally 280vh with sticky h-screen pin — don't flag as bug. Section anchors (#timeline, #comparison) are not present as IDs; sections are still rendered correctly through SectionCut wrappers. Backend tests live at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py and run via `pytest backend/tests/backend_test.py`.
